introduction-when-standard-networking-is.core: Some workloads outgrow internet VPNs and ordinary ENIs: hybrid data centres need consistent, high-bandwidth private links (Direct Connect), security teams need transparent inline inspection by third-party appliances (Gateway Load Balancer), and HPC/ML needs OS-bypass, low-latency interconnects (Elastic Fabric Adapter).

first_principles.problem: A hybrid enterprise sees jittery VPN performance, appliance chokepoints and slow multi-node training.
truths: Inline appliances must scale and be transparent.

analogy.title: Specialist roads
analogy.story: A private freight railway, a customs checkpoint every truck passes through, and a pneumatic tube for urgent parcels.
analogy.breaks: Real infrastructure takes years to build; DX takes weeks, GWLB and EFA minutes.

example.title: Matching need to service
flow: All egress through Palo Alto firewalls → GWLB

check.q: Which service provides OS-bypass networking for MPI and NCCL?

direct-connect-dx-the-physical-layer.core: Direct Connect is a physical fibre cross-connect from your router to AWS at a DX location, giving private, consistent bandwidth (1/10/100 Gbps dedicated or hosted sub-rate) and lower data-transfer-out pricing. Virtual interfaces (private, public, transit) carry BGP sessions to VPCs, AWS public services or Transit Gateways via a DX Gateway.

first_principles.problem: Large nightly data transfers over VPN are slow, unpredictable and expensive.
truths: A single link is a single point of failure.
derivation: Use a **DX Gateway** to reach many VPCs/regions.
Build **redundancy** (two locations, or DX + VPN backup).

analogy.title: A private motorway lane from your warehouse to the port
analogy.story: No public traffic, predictable travel time, but if the lane closes you need another route.
analogy.breaks: A motorway lane is public road; DX traffic isn't encrypted by default, so add MACsec/IPsec if needed.

example.title: Resilient hybrid design
flow: Transit VIFs → DX Gateway → TGWs in 2 regions

check.q: Is Direct Connect traffic encrypted by default?
check.a: No; use MACsec on supported connections or run IPsec VPN over DX.

gateway-load-balancer-gwlb-the-transpare.core: GWLB inserts fleets of third-party virtual appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS) transparently into traffic paths. It operates at layer 3, preserving source/destination IPs, encapsulates packets with GENEVE to appliances, keeps flows sticky to one appliance, health-checks and scales them, and is reached via GWLB endpoints placed in route tables.

first_principles.problem: A single firewall instance chokes throughput and fails as a single point of failure, and NAT hides original IPs.
truths: Flows must stay on the same appliance (stateful).
derivation: **GWLB endpoints** in route tables steer traffic.
**Centralise** in an inspection VPC with TGW.

analogy.title: An airport security lane system
analogy.story: Passengers are routed to any free scanner, keep their identity, and the same scanner handles their whole bag.
analogy.breaks: Passengers know they're being scanned; GWLB is transparent to endpoints.

example.title: Ingress inspection
flow: IGW edge route table → GWLB endpoint

check.q: What protocol does GWLB use to send packets to appliances?

elastic-fabric-adapter-efa-bypassing-the.core: EFA is a network interface that lets HPC and ML apps (MPI, NCCL via libfabric) bypass the kernel and talk directly to the network hardware using AWS's Scalable Reliable Datagram protocol, giving low, consistent latency and high throughput for collective operations across thousands of instances.

first_principles.problem: All-reduce across 64 GPU nodes is limited by TCP latency and kernel overhead.
truths: Kernel network stacks add latency and CPU cost.
SRD spreads packets across many paths.
derivation: Allow **all traffic within the SG** for EFA.

analogy.title: A private pneumatic tube between offices
analogy.story: Messages skip the mailroom entirely and arrive almost instantly.
analogy.breaks: Tubes are point to point; EFA scales to thousands of nodes.

code.text:
fi_info -p efa
# run NCCL all-reduce benchmark across nodes
mpirun -np 16 -x FI_PROVIDER=efa ./all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 4G -f 2
